title: THE PARTNER AND THE MACHINES GLIDE ON THE OTHER SCREEN
why: His answer 2.27 b (no more than 50 ms extra for player 2, with prediction). Every body is sent ten times a second, and the receiving window chased the newest spot with a plain ease, so a walking partner or machine surged to 1.55 times its speed and stalled to 0.57 times inside each tenth of a second, and sat about 130 ms behind. The receiving window now reads each body speed from its last two samples, aims a little ahead of the newest spot (at most 0.12 s, never into a wall) and moves the body at that speed while it eases out the error. Nothing that is sent changes, so the host and the shared thread do no extra work. A body that stops, jumps or rolls fast gets no lead. WATCH IN A PLAYTEST (player 2 screen and the partner on both screens): a body that slides a little past a corner or a stop, then settles back, or a small hop when a machine turns or a door opens; the glide should look steady, with no surge and stall ten times a second.
now: In a two player raid, the partner and the machines on the other screen glide at a steady speed instead of surging and stalling, and sit closer to where they really are.
